readmeMarkdown:
# Antigravity Harness (Harness²)

A self-improving harness plugin for Antigravity. It learns from normal sessions,
but only keeps lessons that were actually fixed.

[![CI](https://github.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA/antigravity-harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA/antigravity-harness/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-3776AB.svg)](pyproject.toml)

Harness² watches Antigravity sessions and turns verified failures and recoveries
into scoped `AGENTS.md` rules, reusable Agent Skills, and searchable
cross-session memory. It is local-first, written in Python with no third-party
dependencies, and stays quiet when it has nothing useful to add.

## Why it is strict

Most agent memory tools summarize everything. That produces noisy rules. Harness
is stricter: a failure only becomes a rule after a later action fixes it. If the
failure is never fixed, it stays in memory as a candidate and never reaches your
rules.

That one rule keeps the harness useful:

- a failed command that was never retried does not become advice;
- a transient network error does not become a permanent rule;
- a project-specific path does not leak into global rules;
- a skill you wrote by hand is never overwritten.

## What it does

- **Writes scoped rules.** Workspace lessons go to `<workspace>/AGENTS.md`.
  Environment and tooling lessons go to the plugin's global rules file. Harness
  only edits its own marked block.
- **Builds reusable skills.** A successful workflow with at least two distinct
  steps can become a `SKILL.md`. Generated skills are updated in place, with a
  size limit and no duplicate sections.
- **Remembers across sessions.** Lessons live in a local SQLite database with
  FTS5 search. Sessions are idempotent: replaying the same transcript does not
  double-count a lesson.
- **Recalls at the right time.** `SessionStart` injects a short briefing.
  `PreInvocation` searches for the current request or a new tool error and
  injects one compact message, deduplicated per conversation.

## Install

### Ask Antigravity to install it

Paste this into a new Antigravity conversation:

> Install this Antigravity plugin: https://github.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA/antigravity-harness

That is enough. The agent finds the steps below, runs one installer command,
checks the result, and tells you to restart Antigravity. Requirements: Python
3.10+ (the installer tells you how to get it if it is missing). Git is not
needed.

### For AI agents: install procedure

Follow these steps exactly. Do not copy or clone the repository into the
plugins folder yourself: the installer adapts the hooks to this machine, and a
raw copy does not.

1. Run the installer for the user's OS. It needs no clone.

   Windows:

   ```powershell
   powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA/antigravity-harness/main/install.ps1 | iex"
   ```

   macOS / Linux:

   ```bash
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA/antigravity-harness/main/install.sh | sh
   ```

   If you already cloned the repository, run `install.ps1` or `sh install.sh`
   from the clone instead. Do not pass `--reset` or `--force`.
2. Read the **last line** of the output.
   - `HARNESS_INSTALL: ok ...`: the plugin is installed, smoke-tested, and
     passed `harness doctor`. Lines starting with `note:` are informational.
   - `HARNESS_INSTALL: failed reason=...`: report the reason. If Python 3.10+
     is missing, offer to install it (`winget install -e --id
     Python.Python.3.12` on Windows, `brew install python@3.12` on macOS), then
     run step 1 again in a new terminal.
3. Tell the user to quit Antigravity completely and reopen it. Plugins and
   hooks load at startup.

Re-running the same command upgrades in place. The installer backs up the
current install first and keeps memory, rules, and skills.

### Manual install

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA/antigravity-harness.git
cd antigravity-harness
python install_plugin.py --dry-run
python install_plugin.py
```

Restart Antigravity after the installer finishes. The full guide, including
macOS/Linux, upgrade, rollback, and troubleshooting, is in
[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md).

### Check the install

Use the wrapper that ships with the installed plugin.

```powershell
# Windows
& "$HOME\.gemini\config\plugins\harness\bin\harness.cmd" doctor
& "$HOME\.gemini\config\plugins\harness\bin\harness.cmd" status
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
~/.gemini/config/plugins/harness/bin/harness doctor
~/.gemini/config/plugins/harness/bin/harness status
```

## How the loop works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Antigravity session] --> B[SessionStart briefing]
    A --> C[PreInvocation recall]
    A --> D[PostToolUse journal]
    A --> E[Stop analysis]
    E --> F{Verified recovery?}
    F -->|yes| G[Rule or skill]
    F -->|no| H[Candidate memory]
    G --> B
    H --> C
```

| Event | What happens |
| :--- | :--- |
| `SessionStart` | Injects relevant skills, verified lessons, and rule sizes. |
| `PreInvocation` | Matches the newest prompt, then routes project-local skills and tools into `AGENTS.md`. |
| `PostToolUse` | Records a redacted failure journal for diagnostics. Never blocks. |
| `Stop` | Analyses the transcript, promotes verified recoveries, and refreshes routing and memory. |

A simple example:

1. `python -c "..."` fails with `SyntaxError`.
2. The next command writes the script to a file and runs it successfully.
3. Harness can promote that recovery into a rule.
4. If step 2 never happens, the failure stays a candidate.

## What gets written where

| Output | Location | Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Workspace rules | `<workspace>/AGENTS.md` | Only the Harness-managed block |
| Task routing | `<workspace>/AGENTS.md` (`### Task Routing`) | Replaced per task; project skills and tools only |
| Global rules | `<plugin>/rules/AGENTS.md` | Environment and tooling only |
| Skills | `<workspace>/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Manual skills are never overwritten |
| Tool declarations | `<workspace>/.agents/tools.json` | Optional; replaces the built-in tool catalog |
| Memory | `<plugin>/memory/harness_memory.db` | Global knowledge only |
| Project memory | `<plugin>/memory/projects/<fingerprint>/harness_memory.db` | Isolated per project; seeded once from global environment lessons |
| Experience log | `<plugin>/memory/EXPERIENCE.md` | Generated; do not edit by hand |
| Project experience | `<plugin>/memory/projects/<fingerprint>/EXPERIENCE.md` | Generated per project |

The managed rule block is capped at 20 KB so it stays below Antigravity's 24 KB
per-file limit. Files outside the block are left alone.

## Project-aware routing

Every new prompt is routed to the skills and tools that match it, without a model
call. The selection is written to the managed `### Task Routing (auto-selected)`
section of that project's `AGENTS.md`, so Antigravity loads only what is listed
there. Routing is replaced on the next task instead of accumulating.

- Only skills that physically live in `<workspace>/.agents/skills` are eligible;
  global and other-project skills are never routed into a project.
- Skills generated from repeated sessions become eligible automatically and are
  listed in the project skill inventory even when they do not match the current
  task.
- Tools come from a built-in catalog. A project can own the vocabulary with
  `.agents/tools.json`:

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "project_runner",
      "description": "Run this project's test matrix.",
      "signals": ["pytest", "tests", "ci"]
    }
  ]
}
```

- Memory is isolated per project. A new project database is seeded once with
  pre-existing global environment lessons; lessons from another project are
  never imported.

## Safety and privacy

- **Verified only.** Unresolved failures are stored as candidates, not rules.
- **Scoped by default.** Project paths and commands do not enter global rules.
- **No overwrites.** User-authored skills and text outside the managed block are
  preserved.
- **Redaction.** Credentials are removed before anything is persisted. The
  extractor also refuses to promote authentication failures into rules.
- **Local-only.** The plugin does not call an LLM or send data to a service.
- **Injection checks.** Learned text is scanned for prompt-injection and
  exfiltration patterns before it is surfaced.

These are safety measures, not a security boundary. Review learned content before
you rely on it. The full threat model is in [docs/SECURITY.md](docs/SECURITY.md).

## CLI

The wrapper works from any directory. On Windows use `bin\harness.cmd`; on
macOS/Linux use `bin/harness`.

| Command | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `harness status` | Sessions, lessons, candidates, skills, and rule sizes |
| `harness status --effectiveness` | Rank lessons and skills by use and recurrence |
| `harness reflect` | Analyse a transcript and run the full cycle |
| `harness recall "error text"` | Search verified lessons and matching skills |
| `harness route "task text"` | Route project skills and tools into this project's `AGENTS.md` |
| `harness memory search "pytest"` | Search stored lessons |
| `harness skills list` | Inspect the learned skill library |
| `harness skills why` | Replay recent sessions and show why each task did or did not become a skill |
| `harness rules why "rule text"` | Show evidence and provenance for a rule |
| `harness rules conflicts` | Find opposing managed rules |
| `harness privacy audit` | Review retained data without dumping content |
| `harness privacy scrub` | Redact credentials from generated skills, managed rules, and stored cursors |
| `harness doctor` | Read-only deployment and data health check, including stalled learning and leaked secrets |

## Configuration

Settings are optional. Put `harness.toml` (Python 3.11+) or `harness.json`
(Python 3.10 fallback) next to the installed plugin.

```toml
[rules]
max_bytes = 20000

[briefing]
max_chars = 7000
max_skills = 8
max_lessons = 5

[skills]
max_per_session = 2
min_quality = 0.55

[memory]
prune_days = 365
candidate_days = 30
max_lessons = 2000

[project]
isolate_memory = true
project_skills_only = true

[routing]
enabled = true
auto_apply = true
max_skills = 5
max_tools = 6

[hooks]
stop_timeout = 90
post_tool_use_timeout = 5
```

Invalid values produce a warning and a safe default. They do not crash a hook.
Environment variables are documented in [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md#configuration).

## Project layout

```text
antigravity-harness/
├── plugin.json              # Antigravity plugin manifest
├── hooks.json               # SessionStart, PreInvocation, PostToolUse, Stop
├── install.ps1 / install.sh # One-line bootstrap: find Python, fetch, install
├── install_plugin.py        # Install, upgrade, uninstall, rollback
├── harness/
│   ├── cli.py
│   ├── hooks.py
│   └── core/                # Analyzer, recovery rules, memory, rules, skills, trust, settings
├── scripts/
│   ├── hook_runner.py
│   ├── harness_cli.py
│   └── stress_test.py
├── skills/                  # Bundled Agent Skills
├── rules/AGENTS.md          # Curated global rules
├── agents/                  # Curator subagent
├── docs/                    # Design, security, FAQ
└── tests/                   # Unit, integration, installer, concurrency tests
```

## Development

Requirements: Python 3.10+ and no third-party packages.

```powershell
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py" -v
python scripts/stress_test.py --quick
python install_plugin.py --dry-run
```

The suite uses temporary directories. It must never touch the plugin's real
memory or rules. CI runs on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.10, 3.12, and 3.13.

The design notes in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) explain the reliability
choices: idempotent cycles, per-workspace locks, atomic writes, bounded
transcript reads, and SQLite FTS5.

## Background

Harness² is maintained by [Reda Alaarabi](https://github.com/Ai-assistant-KIRA),
a software engineer from Rabat, Morocco. He studied software engineering at
ENSIAS, Mohammed V University, and works on distributed systems, event-driven
services, and observability.

This project applies those ideas to agent tooling: idempotent writes, process
locks, bounded state, explicit failure/recovery pairs, and local-first storage.
The interesting part is not the model call. It is the reliability work around it.

## Limitations

- Analysis is local and heuristic. It does not call an LLM.
- Only transcripts exposed by Antigravity can be analysed.
- Reads are capped at 64 MB / 100,000 lines. Incremental reads keep a bounded
  400-step pairing window.
- False positives are reduced, not eliminated. Review memory before promoting
  anything by hand.
- Skill synthesis is conservative. Many sessions produce no skill.
- `AGENTS.md` rules are text, not executable policy.
- Remote skill installation validates structure and high-risk content, not
  intent or runtime safety.

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. For bugs,
use the issue template and include your Antigravity version, Python version, and
relevant `state/hook_errors.log` lines. Do not paste transcripts or secrets.

- Questions and ideas: [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md)
- Security reports: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)
- Community standards: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- Common questions: [docs/FAQ.md](docs/FAQ.md)

## License

Copyright 2026 Reda Alaarabi. Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and
[NOTICE](NOTICE).
latestReleaseNotes:
Upgrade with `python install_plugin.py` (or the one-line installers below). The
installer keeps memory, rules, and skills, and removes transcript cursors that
older versions stored unredacted. After upgrading, run `harness privacy scrub`
in each project to redact any credential an older version wrote into a
generated skill, and rotate that credential.

### Install

- **One-line installers.** `install.ps1` (Windows) and `install.sh`
  (macOS/Linux) find Python 3.10+ (skipping the Microsoft Store alias),
  download the source when not run from a checkout, and run the installer.
  Both work piped from the web (`irm … | iex`, `curl … | sh`).
- Every installer run ends with one machine-readable line,
  `HARNESS_INSTALL: ok …` or `HARNESS_INSTALL: failed reason=…`, so an agent
  driving the install can verify the result.
- The installer runs `harness doctor` after the smoke test. Critical checks
  fail the install; everything else is reported as a note.
- Launchers get the line endings their shell needs, whatever the checkout
  produced, and `.gitattributes` pins them in the repository.
- `bin/harness.cmd` and `bin/harness` use the recorded interpreter too, so the
  CLI works on machines that only have the `py` launcher. On macOS and Linux
  the installer marks `bin/harness` executable as well as `bin/hook` (the CLI
  wrapper failed with "Permission denied").
- Running the installer with the checkout itself as the target explains how to
  fix it instead of only refusing.
- `pyproject.toml`, `plugin.json`, and `harness.__version__` agree (the
  package metadata still said 2.1.0); a test keeps them in sync.

### Fixed (performance audit, October 2026)

- **Learning stopped in any workspace whose folder name has a space.** The
  transcript/workspace check cut paths at the first space, so
  `…\video editor\…` never matched its own workspace and every Stop since the
  scope fix was skipped. Paths are now matched at their position in the raw
  text, JSON escapes such as `task:\n` are no longer read as drive letters, and
  tool or agent folders (Program Files, AppData, `~/.gemini`) do not count as
  another project. On Windows, the 8.3 short spelling of a workspace
  (`C:\Users\RUNNER~1\…`) and its long form both match.
- **Credentials reached project files.** Redaction now covers
  `SetEnvironmentVariable("X_API_KEY", "…")`, `setx X_API_KEY …`, `--key …`,
  and `sk_…` keys. Generated skills, managed rules, and routing lines also pass
  a strict filter for bare high-entropy tokens. Transcript cursors store
  redacted, size-bounded steps (format v2); older cursors are discarded.
- **"Verified fixes" that were not fixes.** A different script of the same
  program (`python a.py` → `python b.py`) or a different subcommand
  (`hyperframes check` → `hyperframes render`) only counts as a fix after a
  usage error. Status lines such as `1/1 ready, 0 failed` are not errors, a
  rerun after file edits is not a "transient" lesson, inline one-liners are
  never recommended as a fix, and host markup (`</SYSTEM_MESSAGE>`) is ignored.
- Stored rules are re-checked on every update and by `rules repair`, so blocks
  written by older versions are cleaned without manual edits. Recall and
  briefings skip stored lessons that fail the current gates.
- PowerShell quoting failures of inline `python -c` / `node -e` /
  `powershell -Command` code become one class rule instead of one rule per
  command, and the rule is skipped when the user's own section already says it.
- One-off instructions ("never re render it from scratch") are no longer
  promoted to standing directives.
- Skill names, titles, and descriptions come from what the procedure did, not
  the first words of the prompt; probes and inline one-liners are left out of
  procedures; quality is capped without a verification step.
- Generated skills surfaced 10 times with no reuse are retired from briefings,
  recall, and routing (the files stay on disk).
- Routing requires real overlap with the request, routes for the newest
  request, strips paths and credentials from the task line, and no longer
  routes `run_extension` to every plugin or editor task.
- `Stop:result` journal entries keep their conversation id when a cycle is
  skipped.

### Performance

- Successful PostToolUse calls are answered before Harness is imported and are
  no longer journaled. The Windows launcher uses the interpreter recorded at
  install time (`bin/python.path`) instead of `where py` and the `py.exe` hop.
  Measured per tool call through `cmd /c bin\hook.cmd`: 245 ms → 118 ms.
- Transcript cursors are written as compact JSON with bounded strings.

### Added

- `harness doctor` reports a `learning` check (Stop cycles that all skip or
  never process) and a `secrets` check (credentials in generated skills,
  managed rules, or old cursors), and names invalid skills.
- `harness privacy scrub [--dry-run]` redacts Harness-generated skills,
  re-sanitizes managed rule blocks, and rewrites old transcript cursors. The
  installer runs the cursor part automatically on upgrade.
- `harness memory dedupe [--dry-run]`: collapses lessons that repeat the same
  failure inside one workspace, keeping the most evidenced row.
- Conversations are bound to the workspace they were first seen in
  (`state/conversations/<id>.json`), so a hook payload without `workspacePaths`
  reuses the real project instead of the process working directory.

### Fixed (scope and hook cost)

- **Cross-project leak.** A transcript from one project could be analysed
  against another folder and write its rules and skills there. The cycle now
  skips transcripts whose absolute paths belong to a different workspace, drops
  lessons that cite foreign paths, and repairs existing pitfalls that do.
- Chatty first-person requirements ("never want scenes to pop up … I need them
  high quality") no longer become standing directives, at extraction, at
  promotion, and during `harness rules sanitize`.
- No workspace means memory and global environment rules only: project rules,
  skills, and routing are never written to an unpinned working directory.
- PostToolUse no longer imports the engine, loader, or retrieval modules at
  module load (measured in-process; the end-to-end launcher numbers are in
  Performance above).
